clauses.reason: Exhausted by performance on its own stated effective date. The order revokes Executive Order No. 1023 of February 6, 1909 and says it becomes effective on the ninetieth day from its date, April 1, 1942; the ninetieth day after April 1 is June 30, 1942, when the revocation took effect and the order had nothing further to command. If the date of the order were counted as day one the date would be June 29, 1942 (alternative reading). Actor: EO 9120 itself.

research_rationale:
EO 9120 (April 1, 1942, Franklin D. Roosevelt), titled Revocation of Executive Order No. 1023, Reserving Land for the Use of the Department of Agriculture; Alaska, read in full in the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9120.txt; 7 FR 2589, PDF pages 3-3; machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, not an authenticated transcription). Identity: the extracted page carries the heading Executive Order 9120, the register title, the date line April 1, 1942, and F.R. page references for the April 4, 1942 issue. The order has one operative command: it revokes Executive Order No. 1023 of February 6, 1909, which reserved land near the town of Rampart, Alaska, as a site for an agricultural experiment station, and it provides that the order becomes effective on the ninetieth day from its date. Date: counting from April 1, 1942 and excluding that day, the ninetieth day is June 30, 1942 (April has 30 days, May 31, June 30). If the day of the order were counted as day one, the ninetieth day would be June 29, 1942; the claim records June 30 and states this alternative. First end: the revocation is self-executing on that date, so the command is exhausted by performance on 1942-06-30. The text of EO 1023 itself was not read; the identity of the revoked order rests on the recital in EO 9120.
